chapter_colophon: इति श्रीदामोदरसूनुना शार्ङ्गधरेण विरचितायां शार्ङ्गधरसंहितायां पूर्वखण्डे रोगगणना नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः॥७॥

sources.name: BharatKosha — Śārṅgadhara Saṃhitā with Dīpikā Hindi commentary
sources.role: primary printed/annotated witness; pages 98-120; explicitly preserves verse 204 and the Pūrva Khaṇḍa colophon

sources.name: Sanskrit Wikisource — Pūrva Khaṇḍa
sources.role: independent Sanskrit witness; cross-check source for the chapter but not treated as complete where extraction is incomplete

source_reconciliation.finding: The printed Dīpikā witness establishes a very large disease-enumeration chapter of 204 numbered verses. BharatKosha pages 98-120 expose the sequence through verse 204 and the closing colophon.
source_reconciliation.important_correction: This chapter is not a short disease list. It systematically enumerates disease groups and subtypes across fever, diarrhoeal/abdominal disorders, respiratory and wasting disorders, urinary/genital disorders, swellings and hernias, wounds and ulcerative conditions, ophthalmic disorders, gynecological/obstetric disorders, and other complications.
source_reconciliation.resolution: Printed Dīpikā 1-204 is the canonical working extent. The complete verse-level Sanskrit layer should be transcribed from the printed scan in a controlled pass; no missing verses are reconstructed from parallel texts.
source_reconciliation.commentary_policy: The Dīpikā explanatory notes sometimes add modern diagnostic analogies (for example thermometer/temperature discussion and possible modern interpretations of selected diseases). These are commentary, not canonical identifications.

verified_opening_and_closing.sanskrit: रोगाणां गणना पूर्वं मुनिभिर्या प्रकीर्तिता । मयात्र प्रोच्यते सैव तद्भेदा बहवो मताः ॥ १ ॥
verified_opening_and_closing.point: The author states that the previously taught enumeration of diseases is being presented, while acknowledging many subdivisions.
Nine types of śotha are enumerated: individual doṣas, paired doṣas, sannipāta, trauma and poison.
Seven types of vṛddhi are enumerated: vāta, pitta, kapha, rakta, medas, mūtra and antravṛddhi.
The chapter continues with a numbered catalogue of penile/urogenital disorders.
Six types of timira are enumerated in the printed witness.
The printed witness introduces eight गर्भजा disorders.

verified_opening_and_closing.sanskrit: इति प्रसिद्धा गणिता ये किलोपद्रवा भुवि । असङ्ख्याश्चापरे धातुमूलजीवादिसम्भवाः ॥ २०४ ॥
verified_opening_and_closing.point: The conclusion distinguishes enumerated well-known disorders from innumerable others arising from dhātu, plant/root and living/non-living sources.

commentary_mapping.coverage: Dīpikā explains why the chapter enumerates diseases rather than supplying full individual symptom descriptions and adds source references.
Dīpikā supplies explanatory disease notes and occasionally modern analogies; these remain attributed commentary.
Dīpikā explains wound and urogenital disease terminology; traditional definitions are preserved without forced modern equivalence.
Dīpikā explains sensory, head and eye disease categories and cites classical parallels.
Dīpikā explains yoni and fetal disease categories, with traditional obstetric terminology.
Dīpikā explains the chapter's closing distinction between enumerated and innumerable disorders and the final Pūrva Khaṇḍa colophon.

assessments.question: शोथ कितने प्रकार का बताया गया है?
वृद्धि के कितने प्रकार गिनाये गये हैं?
ज्वर के दोषज, सन्निपातज, अभिघातज और अभिषंगज वर्गीकरण की संरचना समझाइए।
किसी शास्त्रीय रोग-नाम को आधुनिक रोग के साथ समान मानने से पहले किन स्रोत और परिभाषात्मक सावधानियों की आवश्यकता है?
श्लोक 204 में प्रसिद्ध/गणित रोगों और असंख्य अन्य रोगों के बीच क्या भेद किया गया है?

canonical_import_plan.step_1: Transcribe printed Sanskrit verses 1-204 directly from the verified BharatKosha scans.
canonical_import_plan.step_2: Cross-check the Sanskrit sequence against Wikisource where both witnesses are available.
canonical_import_plan.step_3: Preserve the printed disease-category numbering and do not modernize disease names in the canonical layer.
canonical_import_plan.step_4: Create Hindi translation and student explanations only after canonical Sanskrit locking.
canonical_import_plan.step_5: Map Dīpikā explanations separately, especially where the commentary proposes modern analogies.
canonical_import_plan.step_6: Run chapter-level Sanskrit, translation, commentary, assessment and reader regression tests.
